title: 6-Week Hip Protocol
tagline: Build tolerance • Improve control • Reduce irritation
goal: Build strong, stable, pain-free hips through controlled movement, glute engagement, and core stability.

principles.title: Glute engagement
principles.text: Glutes on, shoulders down, engage core.

principles.title: Frequency
principles.text: Daily. Do all routines EVERY DAY

dailyBasics.title: Posture
dailyBasics.text: Shoulders down, chest tall, core lightly braced.

dailyBasics.title: Glute engagement
dailyBasics.text: Keep glutes lightly engaged at all times.

dailyBasics.title: Core bracing
dailyBasics.text: Brace before every rep (exhale, tighten core as if bracing for a tap).

dailyBasics.title: Breathing
dailyBasics.text: Exhale during effort. Inhale through the nose, exhale through the mouth.

dailyBasics.title: Quality over quantity
dailyBasics.text: Better to do less with perfect control than more with tension or pain.

guidelines: Add 1-2 reps or seconds each week if pain-free.
If pain increases, regress and return to basics.
progression.remember: Small daily habits create big results. Stay consistent, trust the process, and protect today so you can perform tomorrow.
callouts: Pain is a signal, not a goal. Listen to your body. Stay consistent.
Stronger hips. Better movement. For life.
progression.footer: Consistency + Control + Glute engagement + Core bracing = Strong, stable, pain-free hips

exercises.name: Hip Dip (Eccentric Control)
howTo: Stand on a yoga block with the painful side (stabilizing side).
Keep both legs locked (straight) and hips level (no twisting or bending at the hips).
Slowly lower the opposite leg by letting the pelvis drop straight down.
Tap the foot lightly on the floor.
Use a support (wall, chair, counter) to bring the leg back up.
Both legs stay perfectly vertical the entire time.
Do not lean, twist, or hike the hip.
focus: Feel the work in the standing hip and glute.
steps: START: Stand tall on block (painful side).
LOWER (3-5 SEC): Lower opposite leg straight down.
exercises.proTip: Control is the goal. Don't rush the lowering phase.

exercises.name: Side Plank (Modified)
howTo: Lie on your side, elbow under shoulder.
Knees bent and stacked, feet together.
Engage glutes and core.
Lift hips off the ground into a mild side plank.
Exhale and push your air out while holding.
Hold for a few seconds, then lower down with control.
steps: LIFT & HOLD (EXHALE)
LOWER (INHALE)
exercises.proTip: Quality holds build stability. Stop if form breaks.

exercises.name: Knee Drive (For Radiating Pain Only)
exercises.whenToUse: Use only if you have radiating pain down the lateral hip, thigh, leg or even into the calf/foot.
howTo: Stand tall with feet hip-width.
Keep both feet planted.
Engage core and glutes.
Turn (rotate) the knee of the affected side inward and gently drive it toward the opposite knee. (Do not move the foot.)
Keep hips and torso facing forward.
Hold for a moment, then relax.
Repeat as needed.
focus: Do not lift or move the foot.
steps: START: Feet hip-width, knees forward.
DRIVE KNEE IN: Turn knee inward toward opposite knee.
exercises.proTip: Use gently. This is a relief tool, not a strength exercise.

exercises.name: Seated C-Through & Lean
howTo: Sit with feet planted wide and knees bent.
Hands behind your head, elbows out wide.
Rotate your torso in one direction.
Bring that same-side elbow down toward the same-side hip (oblique crunch).
Return elbows to level (not back to start).
Rotate further in the same direction and bring that elbow down again.
Perform 3-4 times, then switch sides.
focus: Rotate through your torso, not just your arms.
Use your obliques to crunch the elbow to the hip.
Keep core engaged and spine tall.
steps: 1. ROTATE: Turn torso in one direction.
2. CRUNCH: Bring same-side elbow to same-side hip (oblique crunch).
3. RETURN & ROTATE MORE: Bring elbows back to level, rotate further, and repeat the crunch.
exercises.proTip: Go only as far as you can maintain control and breath.

exercises.name: Seated C-Through & Lean
howTo: Sit with feet planted wide and knees bent.
Hands behind your head, elbows out wide.
Rotate your torso to one side as far as comfortable.
Bring that elbow toward the same-side hip (oblique crunch).
Return elbows to level (not back to start).
Rotate further in the same direction and repeat the elbow-to-hip crunch.
Perform 3-4 times, then switch sides.
focus: Rotate through your torso, not just your arms.
Use your obliques to crunch the elbow to the hip.
Keep core engaged and spine tall.

2. CRUNCH: Bring elbow to same-side hip.
3. ROTATE MORE: Elbows back to level, rotate further.

exercises.name: Wide Stance Side Reach
howTo: Stand tall with feet wider than hip-width.
Keep legs mostly straight with a slight soft bend in the knees.
Slide your fingers down the lateral line of one leg
as far as you can toward your foot (touching the leg or reaching toward the shoe).
The opposite arm reaches up and over your head to stretch the side.
Return to center.
Alternate sides.
focus: Keep chest up and back flat.
steps: REACH LEFT: Slide fingers down left leg and reach. right arm up.
REACH RIGHT: Slide fingers down right leg and reach. left arm up.
exercises.proTip: Reach, don't rush. Feel the stretch in your oblique.

exercises.name: Hip Leg Pendulum
howTo: Stand on a yoga block with one foot flat and hands supported on a table, bench, or stable surface.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and arms straight.
Keep the standing leg straight (soft knee never bent).
Let the affected leg dangle relaxed.
Slowly swing the leg diagonally across under your body.
Then gently kick it diagonally out behind you (small range, not to full extension).
Control the motion and repeat.
focus: Feel the work in the hip and glute.
exercises.proTip: Control is the goal. Small range, big results.

back and arms straight. straight (knee never bends).
Let the affected leg dangle relaxed.
Slowly swing the leg diagonally across under your body.
Then swing it diagonally out behind you (small range, not to full extension).
Control the motion and repeat.
focus: Feel the work in the hip and glute.
exercises.proTip: Control is the goal. Small range, big results.

exercises.name: 90/90 Seated Stretch Switch
howTo: Sit on the floor with both knees bent to 90 degrees and together to one side.
Feet stay close, knees stacked, both pointing in the same direction.
Without using your hands to push the knees, engage your glutes and adductors.
Shift your hips and rotate both knees to the other side, keeping them stacked.
Push your knees to the floor using hip and inner thigh strength.
Return to the other side and repeat.
focus: Use glutes and adductors to move the knees.
Do NOT use your hands to push.
Keep chest tall and core braced.
steps: START: Knees together to one side.
SWITCH: Engage glutes and adductors to push knees to the other side.
exercises.proTip: Strong hips move you. Control builds them.

exercises.name: Bench Slider Thread & Extend
howTo: Sit on a bench.
One foot stays planted (stable leg).
Place the affected leg's heel on a slider.
Thread the slider between the stable leg and the bench.
Then push the slider straight back behind you into hip extension.
Engage your glute as you extend.
Return forward and repeat.
exercises.proTip: Quality glute engagement > speed or range.

WHAT TO EXPECT:
- Improved hip strength and stability
- Greater range of motion
- Better movement quality
- Less pain and irritation
- Stronger glutes and core connection
- More confidence in daily movement

exercises.name: Wide Sumo Squat
howTo: Stand with feet very wide, toes turned out.
Drive knees apart.
Sit hips down and back, chest tall.
Lower as low as you can with control.
Drive through your heels to stand tall.
Repeat.
exercises.proTip: Depth is less important than control and knee positioning.

exercises.name: Sumo Knee Drop
howTo: Start in a wide sumo squat stance, toes turned out.
Keep one foot planted and rotate the opposite knee down toward the floor.
Lightly touch the knee to the floor.
Drive through the planted foot and glute to stand back up.
Repeat on the other side.
focus: Rotate the knee down with control.
Keep chest tall and core braced.
Drive through the planted leg and glute.
exercises.proTip: Quality movement builds control and hip strength.

exercises.name: Forward Lunge With Hip Extension
howTo: Step forward into a lunge.
Lower hips straight down, both knees bent ~90°.
Drive your hips forward as you stand up.
Squeeze the glute of the back leg at full extension.
Step back and repeat on the same leg.
Complete all reps, then switch legs.
focus: Drive hips forward at the top.
Squeeze the glute of the back leg.
exercises.proTip: Full hip extension = full glute activation.
